papers.title_en: When Does Compensating Inherited Quantization Error Help? Mean-Square Guarantees for Layer-Wise Quantization and Their Limits
papers.evidence: 逐层训练后量化误差补偿的理论分析
papers.tldr: 层间PTQ常用逐层补偿继承量化误差，但其均方保证的成立条件并不清楚。论文在线性网络、可逆校准Gram、零条件均值与共同二阶矩等假设下证明[0,1]固定强度补偿不劣于不补偿，并分解增益来源。作者进一步用ReLU、有界码本和标量反例揭示保证失效机制，并给出残差恒等式。两个8B模型4比特实验显示半强度补偿常优于无补偿，但强度选择仍无稳定规则。
papers.abstract_en: Layer-wise post-training quantization methods let each layer compensate for the quantization error inherited from earlier layers. We ask under what assumptions such compensation guarantees a network output error no larger than without it. For linear networks of any depth, with the required calibration Gram matrices invertible, if the rounding error of each layer has zero conditional mean and a deterministic second-moment map common to both schemes, as under subtractive dither on an unbounded grid, then compensation with strengths in $[0,1]$ fixed in advance gives a mean-square output error no larger than no compensation, each scheme being followed along its own trajectory. The exact gain separates error removed directly from reduced excitation of later rounding noise. Outside this setting the comparison can fail. With rectified linear activations it fails for two independent reasons: noise changes activation states, and, even when no state changes, the correction moves error from samples on which a unit is inactive to samples on which it is active. With stable activations, commutators between the calibration projection and the activation patterns bound the excess. With a bounded codebook, even unique exact layer-wise minimizers with no overload can give a larger output error. For fixed rounding errors it already fails for two scalar linear layers, refuting a published universal guarantee. An exact residual identity gives the necessary and sufficient condition on a common layer input. All these comparisons hold the calibration input fixed. On two 8B models at 4 bits, fixed half-strength compensation beat uncompensated rounding in every model, text and draw tested, yet no rule for choosing the strength beat a layer-wise rule consistently, and lowering the full-network loss on the data used to choose did not reliably lower it on new text.

papers.evidence: 用随机Hadamard变换实现大模型量化投影以降低内存
papers.tldr: 针对大语言模型推理中KV缓存压缩需求，QJL用1比特非对称量化近似保持注意力内积，但稠密高斯投影开销较大。论文提出两种基于随机Hadamard变换组合的快速量化JL构造，第二阶段改用高斯对角而非Rademacher对角。第一种加入高斯抖动平滑量化器，第二种插入随机置换正则化协方差。作者证明其嵌入维度和运行时间保证可比Fast JL，且均可在O(d log d)时间应用。
papers.abstract_en: Quantization has emerged as one of the primary techniques for reducing the memory footprint of large language models during inference. A prominent example is Quantized Johnson$-$Lindenstrauss (QJL), which compresses KV caches using 1-bit asymmetric quantization while approximately preserving the inner products required by the attention mechanism. Recent theoretical and practical work aims at replacing the dense Gaussian projections used by the aforementioned transforms with more structured embeddings $-$ such as compositions of randomized Hadamard transforms $-$ while retaining the same embedding dimension.   In this paper, we introduce two constructions based on a composition of randomized Hadamard transforms, albeit with a Gaussian rather than Rademacher diagonal in the second stage. The first adds Gaussian dithering to smooth the quantizer, while the second inserts a random permutation to regularize the covariance structure of the resulting Gaussian measurements.   We prove embedding-dimension and running-time guarantees analogous to those of Fast JL in the non-quantized setting. The first construction achieves $m=O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(d/δ))$, while the second achieves $m=O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(d/δ))$ under a restriction on $m$. Both constructions can be applied in $O(d\log d)$ time.

papers.title_en: LoopQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Looped Transformers
papers.authors: Zhixiong Zhao, Zukang Xu, Xing Hu, Lifeng Liu, Guangyu Sun, Dawei Yang
papers.evidence: 面向低比特LLM部署的循环感知训练后量化
papers.tldr: 循环语言模型通过复用共享Transformer模块提升参数效率，但递归状态演化使低比特部署面临跨循环激活动态、循环敏感度差异与误差传播等难题。LoopQuant提出循环感知的训练后量化框架，用跨循环分布规范化、交互感知逐循环精度分配和循环条件任务校准协同解决。在Ouro-2.6B上，W4A4性能超过全部W4A8基线，内存降低65.3%，较朴素INT4仅增3.4%存储，解码较BF16加速1.7倍。该工作为低比特LoopLM推理提供了兼顾精度、压缩与效率的实用方案。
papers.abstract_en: Looped Language Models (LoopLMs) improve parameter efficiency by recursively reusing shared Transformer modules, yet their repeated computation over evolving recurrent states poses new challenges for low-bit deployment. Existing post-training quantization (PTQ) methods, largely designed for feed-forward Transformers, fail to account for cross-loop activation dynamics, heterogeneous loop sensitivity, and recursive error propagation, leading to substantial performance degradation at low precision. To address these challenges, we propose LoopQuant, a loop-aware PTQ framework for accurate and efficient low-bit quantization of LoopLMs. LoopQuant is built on three core components: 1) Cross-Loop Distribution Canonicalization (CLDC) learns a shared quantization-friendly representation across recurrent states while preserving parameter sharing; 2) Interaction-Aware Loop-wise Precision Allocation (ILPA) allocates activation precision under a fixed bit budget by modeling task-level loop sensitivity and cross-loop interactions; and 3) Loop-Conditioned Task Calibration (LCTC) further aligns quantized inference with the low-bit recursive trajectory through lightweight task-space calibration. Extensive experiments across LoopLM architectures demonstrate that LoopQuant consistently outperforms existing low-bit PTQ methods. On Ouro-2.6B, LoopQuant under W4A4 surpasses all W4A8 baselines in performance, while reducing model memory by 65.3% with only 3.4% additional storage overhead over naive INT4 and achieving a 1.7 times decoding speedup over BF16. These results demonstrate a strong balance among accuracy, compression, and inference efficiency, providing a practical and deployment-friendly solution for low-bit LoopLM inference. The code is available at [https://github.com/Kishon-zzx/LoopQuant].

papers.title_en: FoveaTree: Information-Density Trees for Query-Guided Visual Token Pruning in Video Large Language Models
papers.authors: Zihan Meng, Weidong Chen, Dexiang Hong, Xinyan Liu, Zhendong Mao
papers.evidence: 视频大模型中的免训练视觉token剪枝与合并
papers.tldr: 视频大模型将每帧编码为数百视觉token，推理成本高；现有剪枝忽略区域层级可压缩性且受注意力漂移影响。FoveaTree提出免训练两阶段剪枝：先用合并增益密度估计与四叉树密度图指导token丢弃、合并和保留，再用注意力树剪枝细化中间层文本到视觉注意力。在InternVL3.5-8B与Qwen3-VL-8B、五个视频问答和一个描述基准上，于50%/30%/10%保留率均取得总体最优，实现更优精度效率权衡。
papers.abstract_en: Video large language models (Video LLMs) encode each frame into hundreds of visual tokens, making video inference expensive. Existing methods reduce this cost through similarity-based merging or attention-based selection but face two challenges: Hierarchy-blind Pruning, which overlooks regional compressibility and can discard critical evidence, and Attention Drift, where positional effects and attention sinks shift text-to-vision attention away from task relevance. We propose FoveaTree, a two-stage, training-free visual-token pruning framework. First, Merge-Gain Density Estimation measures the feature distortion caused by regional merging and constructs a quadtree-derived density map to guide token dropping, merging, and retention. Second, Attention Tree Pruning uses the surviving units and inherited tree topology to refine text-to-vision attention in intermediate LLM layers, preserving relevant regional evidence while removing low-relevance content. We evaluate FoveaTree on InternVL3.5-8B and Qwen3-VL-8B across five video question-answering benchmarks and one captioning benchmark at 50%, 30%, and 10% visual-token retention. FoveaTree consistently achieves overall state-of-the-art performance across the evaluated settings, offering a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

papers.title_en: Bottlenecked semantic compression by representation reconstruction
papers.authors: Xiaoya Tang, Shilong Liu, Daniel Smolyak, Xiwen Li, Quynh Nguyen, Tolga Tasdizen
papers.evidence: 重建引导的视觉token浓缩以减少视觉token数量
papers.tldr: 视觉Transformer处理长视觉token序列时计算开销高，现有方法独立排序并丢弃token，容易损失信息。ReConV用紧凑Summary Bank汇总共享信息，并依据重构残差保留未被充分重建的token。在ImageNet上以少48% GMACs超过未压缩基线，并支持多轮推理复用图像级表示。该框架为视觉token压缩提供了重构引导的新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Vision Transformers incur high computational costs when processing long visual token sequences. Existing reduction methods typically rank tokens independently and discard those deemed unimportant or redundant. We propose a reconstruction-guided framework for visual token condensation (ReConV), which summarizes the complete visual sequence with a compact Summary Bank (SMB) and retains tokens whose information is not adequately captured by the SMB, as indicated by their reconstruction residuals. At each compression layer, a lightweight position-conditioned decoder reconstructs the current tokens, leaving shared information compressed in the SMB while explicitly preserving poorly reconstructed details. Experiments on image classification and multimodal understanding demonstrate favorable performance-efficiency trade-offs: ReConV surpasses the uncompressed baseline with 48\% fewer GMACs on ImageNet and enables reusable image-level representations for efficient multi-turn inference. Code is available at TokenDrop.

papers.title_en: Elephant in the Fridge: Constant-Memory Frame Packing for Long Video Understanding
papers.authors: Shuo Gao, Chenhao Zheng, Zhongzheng Ren
papers.evidence: 以恒定内存将长视频压缩为固定视觉token
papers.tldr: 长视频理解中逐帧编码导致视觉 token 随长度线性增长，显存和延迟难以承受。FramePack-U 是免训练、即插即用的帧打包框架，按文本相关性排序并兼顾多样性，将所选帧以不同分辨率压入固定 token 预算。在 LongVideoBench、MLVU、Video-MME 上，它稳定优于全分辨率与已有 token 压缩/关键帧方法。该工作把长视频理解从 O(n) 扩展转为恒定内存表示，具有简单通用价值。
papers.abstract_en: Hour-long videos, streaming feeds, and movie-length content are pushing vision-language models (VLMs) past their breaking point -- the standard recipe of encoding each frame into visual tokens yields sequences that grow linearly with video length, causing prohibitive memory consumption and inference latency. Existing approaches, such as token reduction and keyframe selection, shorten the token sequence but leave the O(n) scaling intact, failing to resolve the fundamental bottleneck. We propose FramePack-U, a strikingly simple, training-free frame packing framework that compresses arbitrarily long videos into a fixed size visual representation at constant memory cost. FramePack-U requires no fine-tuning or architectural modification -- it plugs directly into off-the-shelf VLMs at inference time. Inspired by FramePack from the generation literature, we propose a content-aware compression strategy for visual understanding under a fixed token budget. Specifically, FramePack-U (1) scores each frame by its semantic similarity to the text prompt and ranks frames in a diversity-driven manner, and (2) packs the selected frames at varying resolutions into a fixed-length context window. This concentrates the memory budget on frames that are both instruction-relevant and visually diverse. While FramePack-U can in theory pack arbitrarily many frames into the fixed budget, we identify an empirical instantiation that generalizes robustly across settings. Extensive experiments on LongVideoBench, MLVU, and Video-MME show that FramePack-U consistently outperforms full-resolution baselines and prior token reduction and keyframe selection methods across diverse model families, parameter scales, and frame budgets. Notably, on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with a 128-frame budget, FramePack-U yields gains of +12.9\%, +10.6\%, and +9.7\% over the official model on the three benchmarks, respectively.

papers.title_en: When 1+1 Backfires: Rethinking Relevance-Diversity Balancing for Sample-Aware Visual Token Reduction
papers.authors: Yihang Huang, Peisong Wen, Chenhao Zhou, Difu Feng, Qianqian Xu
papers.evidence: 面向VLM的视觉token缩减与选择
papers.tldr: 现有视觉 token 压缩常以固定权重平衡文本相关性与视觉多样性，但论文发现最优权重随任务和样本显著变化。作者提出免训练 SAVER，用文本相关 token 的空间集中度构建几何意图先验，推断样本级权重，并结合加权文本质心与视觉边际覆盖增益联合选 token。在 LLaVA-1.5-7B 上仅保留 11.1% 视觉 token 即达全模型 96.5% 性能，并泛化到 LLaVA-NeXT 与 Mini-Gemini。
papers.abstract_en: Visual token compression has emerged as a critical technique for reducing the inference cost of Vision-Language Models. Existing methods select tokens based on text relevance, visual diversity, or a fixed combination of both---treating the relevance-diversity balance as a universal constant independent of the input. We conduct a systematic analysis to challenge this assumption. At the dataset level, grid-searching the optimal relevance-diversity weight per benchmark reveals substantial cross-task variation. More critically, we further maximize per-sample answer likelihood to recover sample-level oracle weights, finding that their distributions not only differ markedly across benchmarks but also exhibit high within-benchmark variance. Based on these observations, we propose SAVER, a framework for Sample-Aware relevance-diversity balanced Visual tokEn Reduction. We first derive a Geometric Intent Prior (GIP) from the spatial concentration of text-relevant tokens to infer a sample-specific relevance-diversity weight, and then apply this weight to jointly select tokens via a Weighted Text Centroid (WTC) for relevance scoring and a Visual Marginal Coverage Gain (VMCG) for diversity. SAVER requires no additional training and achieves sample-aware balancing entirely at inference time. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SAVER consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across diverse benchmarks, retaining 96.5% of full-model performance on LLaVA-1.5-7B with only 11.1% of the original visual tokens, and further generalizing to LLaVA-NeXT and Mini-Gemini.

papers.title_en: WIRE: Weight Space Implicit Representation Encoding of Frozen Video LLMs
papers.authors: Ameen Ali, Tamim Zoabi, Lior Wolf, Chaim Baskin
papers.evidence: 将视频嵌入压缩为临时低秩权重更新，仅保留短视觉上下文
papers.tldr: 长视频使视频语言模型的视觉token过多，prefill、KV cache与生成成本同时上升。WIRE把部分视频条件计算从输入激活迁移到冻结模型权重的临时低秩更新，并用问题条件双向选择性扫描将每帧压缩为少量carrier token。在Qwen3-VL-8B上，16 token/帧使视觉流缩短3.5倍，256/1024帧prefill加速3.35/4.14倍，KV cache同比缩小且解码延迟基本不变。九项256帧基准的平均准确率领先所评估的高效视频语言模型。
papers.abstract_en: Video language models represent a video as a long sequence of visual embeddings in a decoder's input. Every visual embedding is processed by every decoder layer during prefill, stored in the key value cache, and attended by every generated token, so a long video raises prefill, memory, and generation cost at once. We present WIRE (Weight Space Implicit Representation Encoding), which reduces this recurring cost by moving part of the video conditioned computation of a frozen video language model from its input activations into a temporary low rank update of its weights. WIRE keeps a short explicit visual context, so the update acts as a correction rather than a replacement of the video. WIRE first compresses the full resolution embeddings of each frame into a small set of carrier tokens using a question conditioned bidirectional selective scan, and physically contracts the decoder input so every decoder layer, cache entry, and decoding step operates on the shorter sequence. Hypernetworks at selected decoder layers read the compressed forward pass together with a readout of the full resolution features removed by contraction and generate LoRA updates to the attention and feedforward projections. The updates are merged after prefill, so autoregressive decoding runs the unmodified frozen backbone. On Qwen3-VL-8B, WIRE with 16 carrier tokens per frame contracts the visual stream by $3.5\times$, reduces decoder prefill time by $3.35\times$ at 256 frames and $4.14\times$ at 1024 frames, shrinks the key value cache proportionally, and keeps per token decoding latency approximately constant. Across nine benchmark settings at 256 frames, it obtains the highest average accuracy among efficient video language models we evaluate under a common 256 frame budget.
